semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: The text explicitly distinguishes real versus fake from natural versus artificial and gives an example of an artificial tsunami that is still real.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: The authors argue that if intelligence is achieved artificially it will be real intelligence created artificially rather than fake intelligence.
Artificial but not fake is tied to authenticity and to openly non real trees that do not pretend to be natural.
A laboratory setting is called artificial but not fake because incentives and outcomes remain real.
The FCC states that AI technologies generating human voices count as artificial or prerecorded voice and that voice cloning artificially simulates a human voice.
Artificial tears remains the strongest narrowed fake adjacent case.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: Artificial manners remains the strongest sincerity based move toward sham or not genuine.
Researchers describe multilayered artificial skin that more accurately mimics real human skin and quote that it actually looks like real skin.
The same University of Oregon work is summarized as a more realistic artificial skin that mimics real skin.
The review discusses making artificial limbs lifelike and realistic through silicone coverings and sculpted matching.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Voice clones sound realistic but not yet hyperrealistic
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: The study finds that some AI voice clones are judged similarly real and human as human recordings even without a general hyperrealism effect.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Exploring expressivity and emotion with artificial voice and speech technologies
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: Artificial voice is examined as expressive and emotional rather than merely robotic or flat.
Prosthetic eyes are described as looking like a natural eye and as custom made to match the remaining eye.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Can You Get Realistic Fake Teeth
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: Dental prosthetics can closely mimic natural teeth in appearance.
The FCC says voice cloning falls within artificial voice because the technology artificially simulates a human voice.
Medical simulators provide realistic representations of patients and workflows for practice rather than replacement or counterfeit.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: Voice clones sound realistic but not yet hyperrealistic
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: AI voices can be perceived as similarly real to human voices while still being identified as generated or cloned in theory.

semanticMobilityCandidates.sourceName: An artificially simulated outbreak of a respiratory infectious disease
semanticMobilityCandidates.shortSummary: The phrase artificially simulated marks simulation as an intentional modeling operation rather than a broad human made category.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial respiration as mechanical or non-mechanical methods that force air into and out of the lungs; entry terms include mechanical ventilation.
humanRecords.notes: Strong Layer 2 support anchor; semantic mode is sustain/maintain breathing.

humanRecords.year_or_period: MeSH entry term under Respiration, Artificial
humanRecords.short_summary: Mechanical ventilation appears as an entry term under artificial respiration.
humanRecords.notes: Bridge anchor from older artificial respiration to modern life-support technology.

humanRecords.short_summary: MeSH lists Artificial Feeding and Feeding, Artificial as entry terms for nutritional support.
humanRecords.notes: Supports Layer 2 as artificial sustaining necessary bodily intake.

humanRecords.short_summary: Describes artificial nutrition as providing or supplementing daily metabolic requirements when oral feeding is inadequate or contraindicated.
humanRecords.notes: Good support-mode language for the layer label.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines life support care as extraordinary therapeutic measures to sustain and prolong life.
humanRecords.notes: Anchor for artificial keeps life going; phrase 'artificial life support' itself still needs phrase-source review.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial limbs as prosthetic replacements for arms, legs, and parts thereof.
humanRecords.notes: Clean Layer 3 replacement anchor.

humanRecords.short_summary: Explains artificial limbs as prostheses that can replace missing arms or legs and help perform daily activities.
humanRecords.notes: Useful plain-language source for replacement/restoration.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines an artificial heart as a pumping mechanism duplicating natural heart output/rate/pressure and replacing all or part of heart function.
humanRecords.notes: Strong Layer 3 organ-function replacement anchor.

humanRecords.short_summary: Renal dialysis entry notes previous indexing under Kidney, Artificial in 1966.
humanRecords.notes: Strong historical anchor for artificial kidney as replacement therapy context.

humanRecords.short_summary: NLM catalog records a MEDLINE-indexed journal titled Artificial Organs starting in 1977.
humanRecords.notes: Shows field-level consolidation; not a definition by itself.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial insemination as artificial introduction of semen or spermatozoa to facilitate fertilization.
humanRecords.notes: Core Layer 4 continuation anchor; intervention in reproduction rather than support/replacement.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines IVF as assisted reproduction involving direct handling and manipulation of oocytes and sperm to achieve fertilization in vitro.
humanRecords.notes: Strong continuation/reproduction anchor and successor to artificial fertilization language.

humanRecords.source_name: Nature Communications: extra-uterine lamb support system
humanRecords.short_summary: Nature Communications record for the 2017 extra-uterine system work on extreme premature lamb support; useful as artificial womb technology anchor.
humanRecords.notes: Use carefully: animal/preclinical support, not human gestation replacement.

humanRecords.source_name: PubMed: Artificial Womb Technology systematic review
humanRecords.short_summary: 2026 systematic review treats artificial womb technology as preclinical fetal support and notes no human trials yet.
humanRecords.notes: Critical source for controlling speculative status.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial life as computer simulation of life used to study living systems, with recognized field status in the 1980s.
humanRecords.notes: Bridge node from life continuation to computational life-process simulation; do not collapse with reproduction terms.

humanRecords.short_summary: Britannica describes Esperanto as an artificial language constructed in 1887 for international second-language use.
humanRecords.notes: Important non-AI cognition/process anchor: artificial enters human symbolic process before modern AI.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial language as a devised language for international or specific purposes, not native speech.
humanRecords.notes: Useful boundary source for language/process layer.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines AI as computer/robot ability to perform tasks associated with human intellectual processes such as reasoning.
humanRecords.notes: Top-layer anchor, but not chart center.

humanRecords.short_summary: Defines artificial neural networks as computer programs inspired by brain networks, with early theoretical and implementation history.
humanRecords.notes: Cognitive/process modeling node; good bridge from body/organ metaphors to mind process.

humanRecords.short_summary: FCC confirms TCPA restrictions on artificial or prerecorded voice encompass current AI technologies that generate human voices.
humanRecords.notes: Strong modern voice/presence anchor; policy source, not historical origin.

humanRecords.source_name: International Journal of Social Robotics: Artificial companions review
humanRecords.short_summary: Systematic review treats artificial companions as adaptive and engaging systems oriented toward emotional bonds and long-term relationships.
humanRecords.notes: Edge node only; useful for presence layer, not center.

humanRecords.source_name: PubMed: Digital loneliness and AI companions
humanRecords.short_summary: 2024 article frames AI companions in relation to social recognition and digital loneliness.
humanRecords.notes: Use as context only; high risk of making chart too topical.

humanRecords.short_summary: Article explicitly describes artificial consciousness as far from an established discipline and facing theoretical and technological obstacles.
humanRecords.notes: Should be dotted/edge/notes-only unless later evidence justifies display.

humanRecords.short_summary: Britannica frames AGI/strong AI as controversial and out of reach.
humanRecords.notes: AI boundary-control source; likely hover-only or notes-only.

humanRecords.short_summary: Dictionary definition treats AGI as potential capability; first known use listed as 1989.
humanRecords.notes: Useful if the term appears as a dotted edge.

humanRecords.short_summary: Includes artificial limb, artificial respiration, artificial insemination, artificial nutrition and broader made/not-natural senses.
humanRecords.notes: Useful source for why medical/body continuations are part of artificial's definition family.
